chapter: Purple Derby Orchestra on the Gulf Coast
title: Radio broadcast and scrapbook ads: Sanders Beach, Red Cross, Pleasure Palace
summary: From the scrapbook: an Elks Club dance in 1926, a one-time Pensacola radio spot, hotel luncheon jobs and the 1927 Sanders Beach opening.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And the Bithian Sisters Dance, Entertainment and Dance, Monday night, November the 15th, 1926 at the Elks Club from 8 to 12. Assessment of a dollar and a quarter. Ladies free. And then you played on the radio too.
This is the COA Pensacola, huh?
Uh-huh. What's his name called? Roger's Base. No. Not the radio. No, they had the radio.
That's it. That's correct. Johnny Frankel. I didn't call his name to save my life.
How'd you do on the radio? Did you make any money?

We did. No, we didn't. We just played one engagement there, you see. And that was all good. But we had very good luck with it. Our announcer told me, he said, your wife is beautiful. She's coming fine.
Here's the Ratscull. This is at 107 West Gregory.

That's Mobile. That's Grabhouse. And the Merry Gods, you've got again. Chicken Bill is $1. That's expensive. For those days, I guess. They're paying for the music. The Green Room has a New Year's Eve dance beginning at 9 p.m. This must have been a different year. New Year's Night dance beginning at 9 p.m. Scripts. Gentlemen, $2. Fun, Favors, and Frolic. Buffet dance on Wednesday, December the 29th, $2.50. And then New Year's Eve, breakfast and dinner dance, 11 to 6 a.m. $6. That's when you got the $6 on those seven hours.
We didn't have the right price. We said we thought they could pay the pay. That's all.

Oh, yeah. And then here's the Battle House again. The Purple Derby Orchestra has been engaged for the season. It plays at luncheon hours, 12.30 to 2 p.m. So you play lunch, huh? Yeah. And from 6.30 to 8 p.m. at dinner hour, the orchestra will play for the New Year's Eve, celebrate it, fresh in the beginning, 11 p.m. and continue until 6 a.m. and cover charge, $3.00. And then Sanders Beach, you play Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. Grand opening, July the 26th, 1927.

Oh, yeah. So you must have done all right. You played the Florida Town Pavilion for the Red Cross Life Saving Group. The Purple Derby Orchestra. That's out of the scrapbook. Yeah. This Red Cross deal, you got a dollar on a koala. Here's another one for the Sanders Beats. Even had free motion pictures. The New Pleasure Palace in Florida Town. No, they played the party town. No, they played the party town. Oh, Pensacola's New Pleasure Palace. You played there. Here's a script dance. The Swift and Company's office for Andalusia. That's Andalusia. That was a dance, it was it?
